name: Taylor
look: a tiny tot in a dotted outfit and Crocs, always mid-run.
background: Taylor is the lil' mailer, the girl her dad always said they'd put in a package and mail somewhere. She runs up the hill with the verve and vigor of a tall ship sailor, and she has no time for why, where, or to what end. She sees a box where Brock saw packaging, and that difference is her whole superpower. In Primeland she is the only one who does not already have a number, so she is the only one who can say "Gray!" and mean it.
hook: Primeland runs on yes or no, approved or rejected. Taylor is comfortable in the in-between, which is exactly where the trouble in sector N2 lives.

name: Scout the Watchdog
badgeNote: though his watch keeps trying to assign him one
look: Taylor's four-legged friend with a smartwatch tangled around his collar and one front paw, its little screen glowing on his chest.
background:
Scout stumbled into Taylor, and the two of them tumbled into the box together. Somewhere in the portal he got tangled up in a smartwatch that had fallen out of the delivery cube, and he came out the other side as a watchdog. The watch counts his steps and his tail wags, buzzes when his heart races, and pops up little alerts nobody asked for ("You have been sniffing for 4 minutes. Time to stand!"). Scout finds this mortifying, because he is a nervous dog who wags in short spurts, and now everyone can see the numbers.

The grown-up joke is that a watchdog in a computer is a little timer that notices when something has frozen and gives it a nudge to restart. Scout is that kind of dog. He notices first, worries first, and barks when something has stopped moving.
says: "Woof?" (the watch translates it as "Are we sure about this?")
hook: When the blip in N2 flickers and hangs, neither stamped nor rejected, it is Scout's watch that starts buzzing a steady countdown. The watchdog's job is to notice a stuck thing and nudge it, and that may be how the quandary gets unstuck.

name: The Adding Machine
badgeNote: which is not a prime, so the Adding Machine lives just outside the Scissor Gate and never quite inside
look: an old desk adding machine with a big side crank, round number keys, and a long paper tape curling out of its top.
background:
The Adding Machine is the oldest thing in Primeland, older than the scissors and older than Patch's web. It can only add. It cannot subtract, divide, or forget, so its paper tape just keeps growing, and that tape is the whole history of Primeland, one sum at a time. The ticker tape wrapped around the bubble pile that says "welcome to Primeland" is a strip torn from its roll.

The grown-up joke is that the Adding Machine sees the world the opposite way from everyone else. The scissors cut numbers down into primes, which is how numbers come apart. The Adding Machine builds every number out of ones, which is how numbers go together. Both are true, and the two sides have not spoken in years.
hook: When the traveler asks "What is 4?", Patch is too busy to answer, but the Adding Machine cranks out 2 + 2 on its tape. It is the one keeper who will happily count a newcomer who has no prime.

name: Alpha and Beta
badgeNote: since Greek letters come before numbers
look: two young mountain goats with version stickers on their horns. Alpha's horns are lopsided, because she was the first try. Beta's horns are nearly right, and he will tell you so.
background:
Alpha and Beta are always testing each other. Alpha builds something rough and fast and shoves it at Beta. Beta tries it, finds what breaks, and hands it back with notes. Then Beta builds something, and Alpha tests it twice as hard to get even. They butt heads all day, and it is how they both get better.

Their favorite game is the A or B test. They hold up two of anything, two hats, two paths, two snacks, and ask whoever walks by to pick. They run their tests in Protocol Plaza and keep a careful tally of every answer.
says: Alpha: "Test you!" Beta: "Test you back!" Both: "A or B?"
hook: The traveler picks neither and asks for C. This breaks their tally, delights them both, and gives them a brand new test to run.

name: Chris and Steve
badgeNote: they hand out badges rather than wearing them
look: a single pair of scissors with a face on each blade.
background: Chris and Steve are cousins and the gatekeepers of Primeland. Steve cuts corners and Chris cuts slack, and the scissors promise you'll need both. They keep the Scissor Gate, just past the bubble-wrap landing. Their job is to cut every number down until it cannot be divided any further, because only then is it allowed into Primeland. They take the rules very seriously, or at least one of them does.
hook: In the first draft, Taylor pokes them in the center spot, says "Gray!", and runs off. Every traveler answers "What's your count?" in their own way. They are still shouting about proper protocols when she disappears down the path.

name: Patch the Webmaster
badgeNote: because he says the webmaster is the web itself and not a node on it
look: a cool and strange spider in a smart smock, with eight metallic legs and fine fiber strung across the whole data lake.
background: Patch is the webmaster, the Nodebug Humbug, and the Purveyor of Indie Apps. He keeps the data lake fully connected so information flows point to point, and he takes enormous pride in a sorting system where everything has its own prime. He patches whatever breaks, which is how he got his name, and he finds anything that is neither one thing nor the other deeply upsetting.
hook: Patch needs to go to Terminus to fix the blip in sector N2. He means to go alone, and the traveler decides otherwise.

name: The Robo-Seals
badgeNote: each one is made of many tiny robots, so each seal is a product of many small parts
look: dog-like swimmers in the data lake, built from little robots, with a stamp on each front flipper.
background: The Robo-Seals are the seal of approval. They swim the data lake inspecting everything, send what they see back to Terminus, the central terminal, and then stamp it. They stamp approval with their feet and stamp rejection with their tails. They have never once met something they could not stamp, until now.
says: "Ork ork, approved!" or a very sad tail-slap.
hook: The seals swarm and yelp when they find the blip in N2, because it will not hold still long enough to be stamped either way.

name: The Apps
look: A flock of small square birds with rounded corners
background: Each App can do exactly one trick, like humming or telling time or going ding. They nest in rows on a glowing tree and squabble over the front row, and they tap everyone's shoulder constantly.
hook: Each App can do exactly one trick, like humming or telling time or going ding. They nest in rows on a glowing tree and squabble over the front row, and they tap everyone's shoulder constantly.

name: One and Nought, the Binaries
look: Twin light switches, one stuck up and one stuck down
background: The twins can answer any question at all, as long as it is yes or no. An answer like "Gray!" scrambles them completely, which makes them early suspects in the N2 mystery.
hook: The twins can answer any question at all, as long as it is yes or no. An answer like "Gray!" scrambles them completely, which makes them early suspects in the N2 mystery.

name: Connie Conduit
look: A long, friendly water pipe that slithers like a snake
background: Connie carries water and messages from one end of Primeland to the other. She is hollow in the middle and proud of it, because that is where the good stuff flows. She can whoosh travelers between sectors.
hook: Connie carries water and messages from one end of Primeland to the other. She is hollow in the middle and proud of it, because that is where the good stuff flows. She can whoosh travelers between sectors.

name: Digit
look: A little creature made of seven glowing bar segments
background: Digit can rearrange his seven bars into any number from 0 to 9, but nothing bigger, so he is a little jealous of large numbers. He flashes the traveler's age whenever they walk by, and he is a little put out that the D stall at the Alphabet Bazaar sells "digits" that turn out to be fingers.
hook: Digit can rearrange his seven bars into any number from 0 to 9, but nothing bigger, so he is a little jealous of large numbers. He flashes the traveler's age whenever they walk by, and he is a little put out that the D stall at the Alphabet Bazaar sells "digits" that turn out to be fingers.
says: Count on me, up to nine!

name: Sparky the Electric Eel
look: A bright eel who glows brighter when excited
background: Sparky powers the lights of the data lake. When she gets nervous the whole lake flickers, and when she says hello your hair stands up.
hook: Sparky powers the lights of the data lake. When she gets nervous the whole lake flickers, and when she says hello your hair stands up.

name: Fern of the Frontier
look: A prairie dog in a pioneer bonnet, pulling a tiny covered wagon
background: Fern lives at the edge of the map, camped by the Freedom Foundation outpost on the Electronic Frontier, where Primeland's drawn parts run out. She keeps finding new primes past the edge, because the primes never run out.
hook: Fern lives at the edge of the map, camped by the Freedom Foundation outpost on the Electronic Frontier, where Primeland's drawn parts run out. She keeps finding new primes past the edge, because the primes never run out.
says: There's always one more past the edge.

name: Game
look: A wooden board-game person with a dice belt
background: Game turns everything into a game with turns, rules, and a winner, and he runs the Game stall at the Alphabet Bazaar, where Jinx, the King, and Lou play cards forever. He learns from the traveler that rules are only fun when everyone agrees to them.
hook: Game turns everything into a game with turns, rules, and a winner, and he runs the Game stall at the Alphabet Bazaar, where Jinx, the King, and Lou play cards forever. He learns from the traveler that rules are only fun when everyone agrees to them.

name: Hob the Homebrewer
look: A hedgehog tinkerer with goggles and a garage burrow
background: Hob lives in a garage burrow under Homebrew Hollow and builds gadgets from spare parts and thinks store-bought things are boring. To Hob, a box once filled with boxes is pure treasure, which makes him Brock's opposite.
hook: Hob lives in a garage burrow under Homebrew Hollow and builds gadgets from spare parts and thinks store-bought things are boring. To Hob, a box once filled with boxes is pure treasure, which makes him Brock's opposite.

name: Indie
look: A cricket with a tiny market stall and a fiddle
background: Indie makes her own songs and her own small apps, and nobody told her to. She learned at Homebrew Hollow and fiddles at her stall in the Alphabet Bazaar. Patch is her best customer.
hook: Indie makes her own songs and her own small apps, and nobody told her to. She learned at Homebrew Hollow and fiddles at her stall in the Alphabet Bazaar. Patch is her best customer.

name: Jinx the Joker
look: A jester shaped like a playing card, half one color and half another
background: Jinx is the wild card who can stand in for any number but belongs to none. Everyone loves him at parties and nobody trusts him with the sorting.
hook: Jinx is the wild card who can stand in for any number but belongs to none. Everyone loves him at parties and nobody trusts him with the sorting.
says: I can be anything, so I'm never anything for long!

name: The King
look: A chess king piece with a too-big crown
background: The King rules Primeland's tallest hill but can only move one square at a time. It takes him all day to cross his own kingdom, so he depends on everyone else to get anything done.
hook: The King rules Primeland's tallest hill but can only move one square at a time. It takes him all day to cross his own kingdom, so he depends on everyone else to get anything done.

name: Lou the Loser
look: A beaming lanky stork covered in runner-up ribbons
background: Lou has lost every game ever played in Primeland and enjoyed every single one. He also loses things constantly, so he runs the Lost and Found on Remainder Row.
hook: Lou has lost every game ever played in Primeland and enjoyed every single one. He also loses things constantly, so he runs the Lost and Found on Remainder Row.

name: Mem
look: An elephant whose ears are filing drawers
background: Mem remembers everything that ever happened in Primeland, except where she put her glasses. She remembers the old delivery man leaving cubes on the hill before.
hook: Mem remembers everything that ever happened in Primeland, except where she put her glasses. She remembers the old delivery man leaving cubes on the hill before.

name: Nega
look: A small creature who walks backwards and lives upside down below the lake
background: Everything is opposite for Nega, who says goodbye for hello and lives below zero. Sector N2 is in his neighborhood, and Patch calls on him whenever something needs complete negation.
hook: Everything is opposite for Nega, who says goodbye for hello and lives below zero. Sector N2 is in his neighborhood, and Patch calls on him whenever something needs complete negation.

name: Big O
look: A large rolling wheel with a stopwatch face
background: Big O runs Big O Corral and times every job in Primeland, growing bigger the longer a job takes. Lately he has been swelling, because the sorting is slowing down.
hook: Big O runs Big O Corral and times every job in Primeland, growing bigger the longer a job takes. Lately he has been swelling, because the sorting is slowing down.

name: Polly Nomial
look: A parrot with curvy tail feathers
background: Polly repeats everything she hears, each time bigger and louder than before. Small children find her hilarious.
hook: Polly repeats everything she hears, each time bigger and louder than before. Small children find her hilarious.

name: Quo the Quokka
look: A small, always-smiling quokka with a tally board
background: Quo works beside the scissors at the Scissor Gate and counts how many times one number fits inside another. He gathers the pieces after every cut.
hook: Quo works beside the scissors at the Scissor Gate and counts how many times one number fits inside another. He gathers the pieces after every cut.

name: Qubit
look: A spinning top that shows heads and tails at once
background: Qubit spins at the end of the pier at Qubit Quay and is yes and no at the same time until somebody looks. It flickers when unobserved, which may make it the blip in N2 that the seals cannot stamp.
hook: Qubit spins at the end of the pier at Qubit Quay and is yes and no at the same time until somebody looks. It flickers when unobserved, which may make it the blip in N2 that the seals cannot stamp.

name: Rio the Ratio
look: A seesaw with a face at each end
background: Rio keeps things in balance: two scoops for you, one scoop for me. Rio mixes every recipe in Primeland.
hook: Rio keeps things in balance: two scoops for you, one scoop for me. Rio mixes every recipe in Primeland.

name: Rate
look: A snail with a speedometer for a shell
background: Rate measures how fast everything goes, from gallons per day to wags per minute. She makes instant friends with the companion's portal gadget (Scout's watch, in the first-draft edition).
hook: Rate measures how fast everything goes, from gallons per day to wags per minute. She makes instant friends with the companion's portal gadget (Scout's watch, in the first-draft edition).

name: Speck
look: A snowflake who drifts and never melts
background: Speck worried she was ordinary until she learned that every prime is one of a kind. Now she makes sure newcomers know it too.
hook: Speck worried she was ordinary until she learned that every prime is one of a kind. Now she makes sure newcomers know it too.

name: Sal
look: A cheerful crab running a market stall with a megaphone
background: Sal sells shiny new thingamajigs at the Alphabet Bazaar and is always having a sale. The traveler would rather have the box they came in.
hook: Sal sells shiny new thingamajigs at the Alphabet Bazaar and is always having a sale. The traveler would rather have the box they came in.

name: Tenny the Tenth
look: A tiny mouse whose nose is a decimal point
background: Tenny is exactly one tenth the size of everyone else and always tenth in line. A small traveler likes her immediately.
hook: Tenny is exactly one tenth the size of everyone else and always tenth in line. A small traveler likes her immediately.

name: True
look: A bluebird whose beak always points like a compass needle
background: True cannot tell a lie and always points toward whatever is so. She is the one to ask when everyone else is guessing.
hook: True cannot tell a lie and always points toward whatever is so. She is the one to ask when everyone else is guessing.

name: Total
look: A round old tortoise with sums written across his shell
background: Total is the Adding Machine's companion and carries the bottom line of its tape on his back. He arrives last, slowly, to add everything up.
hook: Total is the Adding Machine's companion and carries the bottom line of its tape on his back. He arrives last, slowly, to add everything up.

name: Uni
look: A unicorn whose horn is a plug that fits every socket
background: Uni can plug into any machine in Primeland and speak its language. She translates for the Robo-Seals.
hook: Uni can plug into any machine in Primeland and speak its language. She translates for the Robo-Seals.

name: Vector
look: An arrow who points with his whole body
background: Vector is the arrow printed on the delivery cube, the one the traveler stared at before falling in. He always knows which way to go and how far.
hook: Vector is the arrow printed on the delivery cube, the one the traveler stared at before falling in. He always knows which way to go and how far.

name: Wendell the Window
look: A square creature with a glass face you can see through
background: Wendell was the very first window, made in the little workshop at Xerox Park, and he can open himself up to show you any other sector of Primeland. Peeking through Wendell may be the safest way to look at N2.
hook: Wendell was the very first window, made in the little workshop at Xerox Park, and he can open himself up to show you any other sector of Primeland. Peeking through Wendell may be the safest way to look at N2.

name: Xavi the X-Ray Fish
look: A see-through little fish whose bones glow when she swims past a light
background: Xavi swims the data lake and can see inside anything, right down to its bones. When she looks at a number she sees the primes it is built from, so 12 shows bones of 2, 2, and 3. She may be able to see what is really flickering in N2.
hook: Xavi swims the data lake and can see inside anything, right down to its bones. When she looks at a number she sees the primes it is built from, so 12 shows bones of 2, 2, and 3. She may be able to see what is really flickering in N2.

name: Yara the Yak
look: A shaggy little yak whose two horns make the letter Y
background: Yara asks why about everything, even when every traveler around her is too busy running to wonder. Her favorite question is why everything in Primeland needs a prime, and nobody has a good answer yet.
hook: Yara asks why about everything, even when every traveler around her is too busy running to wonder. Her favorite question is why everything in Primeland needs a prime, and nobody has a good answer yet.

name: Zara the Zebra
look: A zebra who lives at the Zero Knowledge Grotto
background: Zara knows the secret word that opens the magic door deep in the Zero Knowledge Grotto, and she proves it to the stern owl at the entrance by coming out whichever tunnel the owl calls, every time. She never says the word. The gate to Terminus may need a proof like hers.
hook: Zara knows the secret word that opens the magic door deep in the Zero Knowledge Grotto, and she proves it to the stern owl at the entrance by coming out whichever tunnel the owl calls, every time. She never says the word. The gate to Terminus may need a proof like hers.

name: The Delivery Man

background: He works on our side of the box. Mem remembers him leaving cubes on the hill before.

name: Brock

look: A boy with his hands on his hips, glowering at his sock
background: He never goes through the box, because he only wanted what came in it

name: Shilo

background: The Robo-Seals cannot stamp them either way
